options.description: What to put in order, in the order it starts in. A choice marked `disabled` is pinned: it keeps its place in the list, cannot be picked up, and the rows around it move past it.
options.name: choices

options.description: Asks with plain lines in and lines out rather than a region that redraws, for a screen reader: the question is written once, what is typed is echoed where it is typed, and nothing already written is ever moved or erased.
options.name: accessible

options.description: Whether Escape leaves the prompt to go back a step. Defaults to `false`, where Escape does nothing, as it always has.
options.name: back

options.description: Which row starts highlighted, by index into `choices`. Defaults to 0. A disabled choice is passed over for the next one that can be moved.
options.name: initial

options.description: Whether the highlight wraps from one end of the list to the other. Defaults to `true`. A row being carried never wraps, whatever this says.
options.name: loop

options.description: The input router to read keys through. One is built if not given.
options.name: router

options.description: How many rows the list may take. Defaults to what the terminal has left under the question.
options.default: what the terminal has left under the question
options.name: rows

options.description: Gives the prompt up when this aborts, the way Ctrl-C does.
options.name: signal

options.description: Where keys come from. Defaults to the terminal's input.
options.name: stdin

options.description: An answer to start from: the order the list opens in. The rows it names come first, in its order, and the rest after them in theirs; a pinned row keeps its place either way, and a value no movable row holds is dropped.
options.name: value

registryDescription: A sort prompt: pick a row up and move it to put a list in order
